note: D8 r1/r2 are one moment (kept once at 42:37). r2's D14 row is really the plural slip (D15); D14 is kept as r1's C3 'best first' prompt at 1:05:57 and D15 as the A9 plural at 1:06:01. D11 is the same moment as agreed A48 (its right already says نار هادية). D29 dropped as a self-fix: he said ما كان at 40:10 and her line ends 'صح', confirming him. No agreed row challenged.

row.why: Asked which season it is (Sept 21) he offered ربيع (spring, a word he knows - 'ربيع is spring'); she said 'مش ربيع، لا' and at 06:37 supplied خريف (sheet: autumn / fall | 5areef | خريف) - a wrong word with an explicit no, so tier 1 rather than a pure didn't-know.

rulings.why: Real: explicit no to the wrong season word; tier 1 because he produced a different known word, not silence.

row.why: مدينة is feminine so the adjective should be هادية (my reading); Amal was distracted by the sirens and did not address it.

rulings.why: Real gender slip on the adjective, let pass.

row.why: Talking about a past craving (the pizza he ate today) her recast adds كان, the same كان she used in her question at 15:48 / 16:02; he repeated only the على بالي part (agreed A16 covers the vocab piece).

rulings.why: Different piece from A16 (the missing past كان); her recast voiced it.

row.why: The noun phrase needs el- on the adjective too (she had just said بحب البحري / الفلفل الحلو at 17:59); not addressed this time - a new phrase, not a repeat of the fixed one. بهري for بحري is S4.

rulings.why: Real el- slip on the adjective, let pass.
Not a slip: he was asking how to say 'something is wrong with it' (29:03 'how do I say...', 29:34 'فيه or') and Amal answered his question - a question about the form, not a use.

row.why: Repeating her بيهمنا he said بيهنّا; she corrected 'بهم، بيهمنا' - the word is on her sheet ('it matters | Beyhemm | بيهم', 'i matter | Bahemm | بهم'), so a wrong form of a sheet word, not a new word.

rulings.why: Real listening repeat error; tier 2 because the word is on her sheet.
Not an error: بتبيع الرز is fine; Amal's بتبيعه is an alternative, and 15 s later she shows both forms are fine ('بتغسل الرز' -> 'أو بتغسله يعني').

row.medi_said: u marat ana lama ana kasul ana... / لما أنا كسول، Wait.

rulings.why: Both readers saw the same slip; one row at the first line (42:48 is the same moment).

row.why: He built a wrong form ساعية of a word he knows; Amal recast ثلث ساعة and he repeated it twice.

rulings.why: Real wrong form of a known word, recast by her.

row.medi_said: Or برجع الـ الرز في الـ طنجرة.
row.amal_said: Or برجع أحط الرز. ... برجع أحطه أو برجعه ... برجّع.
row.why: برجع (I go back) cannot take the rice as an object; Amal gave برجع أحط and at 45:57 named the doubled برجّع (make-X) - a soft 'Or' fix, so low.
row.english: I put the rice back in the pot

rulings.why: Real: intransitive برجع used with an object; she supplied both repairs including the doubled form.
Duplicate of agreed A48 (51:08 هادي نار -> نار هادية): 51:12 is his repeat of the line she was fixing, within 4 s, and he said هادية himself as she did; A48's right already carries the feminine.

row.why: For 'the bottom part of the rice' Amal recast الرز من تحت and at 52:45 explained تحت الرز means what is under the rice - the preposition's job (ta7et = under vs min ta7et = from the bottom), D1; he repeated it (and slipped again at 52:40, re-fixed - same moment).

rulings.why: Same slip for both readers; D1 fits (which job the preposition does), no need to PROPOSE.

row.medi_said: uh, awali is, awali is country, right?

row.why: Saying 'the best Persian restaurants' he started with the noun; Amal prompted 'The best first' and he put أحسن before the noun (comparative goes in front, as in agreed A57).

rulings.why: r1's row is the real word-order prompt; r2's row here is the plural slip, kept as D15.

row.chat: a7san ma6aa3em Iranyeen fi el-denia fi UAE

Self-fix: Amal's prompt was only about the plural ('Restaurants.'); he dropped the wrong el- on the adjective himself in مطاعم إيرانيين, and nothing she voiced touched it (chat alone is not a correction).

row.medi_said: مين بيدفع؟ Hold on. مين بيدفع؟ Who pays?
row.why: He repeated her question 'مين بيفتح' as مين بيدفع (who pays) - a different known word; she corrected 'Opens، بيفتح'.

rulings.why: Real listening slip; a different lexical item, so tier 1.

Not a vocab slip: he meant 'take' - at 1:07:06 he explained 'It's past tense. They took' and went on أخدوا أحسن مطبخ من إيران; her بيفتحوا steered back to her own question rather than fixing his word.

row.english: they took the best chefs from Iran

rulings.why: Plausible let-pass wrong word, low confidence; goes to Amal's review.
Self-raised question: he asked himself 'Would I say إيرانيين؟' (the right plural) before any help and Amal never answered - a question about the form / self-fix, not a slip.

row.why: He meant 'the Arabs' (1:08:27 'the food is mainly for the Arabs'); the people plural is العرب, العربيين is an invented plural of عربي (sheet: arabic / arab | 3arabi | عربي) - my reading, let pass.

rulings.why: Likely invented plural pattern, let pass; low.

row.medi_said: الأكل مفضل في UAE, uh, أكل إيراني

row.english: the favourite food in the UAE is Iranian food

row.why: Trying the phrase taught at 58:02 he said منك (from you) for معك; Amal laughed and recast معك حق, he repeated 'معك حق. with you' - low because a ن/ع swap could be the engine.

rulings.why: Her laugh and recast show a wrong form of the taught phrase; low for possible mishearing.

row.medi_said: نحتاج، um, jacket. / We only have thirty days that we need a jacket
row.amal_said: آه، يعني نحتاج الـ jacket إندم. ... on them، بس يعني إندم in Arabic.

row.english: thirty days in which we need a jacket

row.why: ra7 takes a bare verb (أقدر) and he kept the b-; Amal let it pass with mm-hmm (her chat drops ra7: ba2dar adfa3).
